evidence: Cic. Brut. 48: lentus in dīcendō, drawling (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly “pliant, tough”; then slow and sluggish, lingering, unhurried (adverb lentē). Traupman also gives it for “backward (mentally)”, a sense we have not found in Lewis & Short; for slow of mind, tardus (see slow to learn).

evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.24.35: vēlōx an tardus sit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain opposite of vēlōx, of motion and action, and also of minds (see slow to learn).

sources: Lewis & Short: lentus · Lewis & Short: tardus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
